{{Quote|Who designed those Sith uniforms? A blind Rodian with a sick sense of humor?|Mission Vao to her captor|<ref name="kotor" />}}
'''Sith trooper armor''', also called '''Sith battle armor''', was the distinctive suit of [[Armor/Legends|armor]] worn by the [[Sith trooper (Sith Empire)|Sith troopers]] of [[Darth/Legends|Darth]] [[Revan/Legends|Revan]] and [[Darth Malak]]'s [[Darth Revan's Sith Empire|Sith Empire]] and later [[Sith Empire (disambiguation)|Sith Empires]]. With its reflective styling and black face mask, it proved an intimidating part of the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] war effort against the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]]. When the war ended, the armor would continue to see use by remnants of the Sith Empire during the [[Dark Wars]], commanded by the [[Sith Triumvirate]] of Darths [[Kreia|Traya]], [[Darth Sion|Sion]] and [[Darth Nihilus|Nihilus]]. Sith troopers with different armor were later employed during the [[Great Galactic War]] and the [[New Sith Wars]].

==Characteristics==
[[File:SithTrooper-TOR.jpg|thumb|left|180px|A Sith trooper during the [[Great Galactic War]]]]
The armor, while bearing the same level of protection and functionality as that utilized by the forces of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] during the [[Jedi Civil War]], was designed specifically to induce fear in opponents. The armor casing, made up of several plates of hard material over a black [[Body glove/Legends|body glove]], was emphasized; the trooper's face was completely obscured from view by a one-way visor, creating the impression of a faceless enemy (a disturbing attribute when the wearer spoke). Though the vast majority of [[Sith trooper (Sith Empire)|Sith troopers]] wore armor that bore a distinctive reflective silver sheen, higher ranks were denoted by armor that was painted in a semi-gloss crimson hue.<ref name="kotor" /> This organizational approach would continue within the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] remnants commanded by the [[Sith Triumvirate]] of [[Darth/Legends|Darths]] [[Kreia|Traya]], [[Darth Sion|Sion]], and [[Darth Nihilus|Nihilus]] during the [[First Jedi Purge]], with elite commandos outfitted in copper version of the armor.<ref name="kotor2" /> The armor of Sith Troopers of the Triumvirate were later seen during the Great Galactic War, including golden and ventilated variants.

==History==
Created for the troops of the [[Darth Revan's Sith Empire|Sith Empire]] by the new [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]], a former [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] named [[Revan/Legends|Revan]], the armor would see widespread use throughout the pan-galactic conflict as veterans of the [[Mandalorian Wars]], bolstered by volunteers from numerous conquered worlds, waged war against the Republic. When [[Darth Malak]] took over the conduct of the war following the capture of Revan by the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]], the war, and use of this type of armor, continued. When the amnesiac Revan, along with Republic officer [[Carth Onasi]] ended up on the Sith-occupied [[Planet/Legends|planet]] of [[Taris/Legends|Taris]] after the ''[[Endar Spire]]'' was [[Attack on the Endar Spire|destroyed]], they were forced to steal a set of Sith trooper armor in order to access the [[Lower City]]. After arriving via elevator, they were subsequently set upon by a number of belligerent [[Black Vulkars/Legends|Black Vulkar]] [[Swoop gang/Legends|swoop gang]] members. The armor was later traded away to [[Hidden Beks|Hidden Bek]] gang leader [[Gadon Thek]] in return for authorization papers that would allow Revan and Carth access to the [[Undercity (Taris)|Undercity]].<ref name="kotor" />

During the First Jedi Purge, the [[Sith Triumvirate]] gathered and led the remnants of Revan's old Sith Empire, including many troopers who had retained their armor. Sith Commandos, an elite offshoot of the regular trooper ranks that served aboard [[Warship/Legends|warships]] such as the [[Ravager (Centurion-class)|''Ravager'']], [[Darth Nihilus]]' [[Flagship/Legends|flagship]], were distinguished by their reflective copper-colored armor.<ref name="kotor2">''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords]]''</ref>

Sith troopers were also a part of [[Imperial Military (Sith Empire)|Imperial Military]] of the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|Sith Empire]] during the [[Great Galactic War]] and the [[Cold War (Galactic Republic–Sith Empire)|Cold War]]. They wore black armor with red stripes on their helmets and shoulder pads.<ref name="ToC" />

[[File:DaimanSithTroopers.jpg|thumb|right|180px|Sith troopers and trooper commanders of [[Daimanate]]]]
During the [[New Sith Wars]] most of [[Daimanate]]'s Sith troopers wore dark blue armor with red dots on their helmets, while Sith trooper commanders had red stripes on their armor. A presumed leader of [[Daiman]]'s Sith troopers wore scarlet red armor.<ref name="Errant4">[[Knight Errant 4|''Knight Errant'' 4]]</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Sith_trooper_concept_art.jpg|thumb|Sith trooper armor concept art.]]
Sith trooper armor was first introduced in the computer and video game ''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic]]'' developed by [[BioWare]], and again in its sequel, ''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords]]''.

The suit of Sith armor acquired by the player in the Taris segment of the story within the first game effects a number of minor changes in the dialogue of many minor characters. While dressed in the armor, the player is indistinguishable from occupying Sith forces. Like all other troopers wearing the armor and thus considered "on duty", the player is not allowed to enter the [[Upper City Cantina]], [[Javyar's Cantina]], or the Hidden Beks' base, though in the latter case this is due to Bek hostility rather than Sith policy. The player is also treated as though he or she were a member of the occupying force by ordinary citizens, who will act deferentially; in addition, patrolling Sith soldiers in the [[Upper City]] will grumble idly about "patrol duty".<ref name="kotor" /> The trade with Thek of the armor in exchange for authorization papers is required in order to advance the plot. However, it is possible to perform a glitch to keep the armor, but still get the papers from Gadon. All that is needed to do is to put the armor on Carth, then remove him from the party. Proceed to Gadon and get the papers, then add Carth back to the party. Strip Carth of his Sith armor and put it on, and you can wear it for the rest of the game, though it will automatically be removed from your inventory once you've arrived on [[Dantooine/Legends|Dantooine]], along with any other Taris quest items.<ref name="guide">[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic: Prima's Official Strategy Guide|''Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic'': Prima's Official Strategy Guide]]</ref>
